v.title: Fernandes Says United’s Contract Talks Are on Pause Until the Red Devils Win Again
v.excerpt: Fernandes says United’s contract talks are on hold until the club wins again, prioritising silverware over paperwork.
v.body:
## Quick take
Bruno Fernandes confirmed that Manchester United have offered him a new contract, but talks are on hold because the club must return to winning ways first. The midfielder’s priority is silverware, not paperwork.

## What happened
Fernandes told ESPN that United’s board had reached out with a contract extension, but he declined to discuss details publicly. He emphasised that the club’s focus should be on regaining the Premier League title, suggesting that performance, not contracts, should drive negotiations.

The player’s comments come amid a season where United have struggled to maintain consistency under Mauricio Pochettino. Fernandes, who has been the team's creative engine, feels the club’s recent results do not justify a contract renewal. He hinted that he will remain at the club if the team can deliver results, but will be open to other opportunities if the situation does not improve.

## Why it matters
- **For Barcelona**: A top talent like Fernandes staying at United keeps the Premier League competitive, meaning we’ll see more high‑profile clashes that could influence our own transfer market strategy. If he stays, it may signal that United will invest more in squad depth, potentially affecting the balance of power in Europe.
- **For Fernandes**: The midfielder’s stance underscores his ambition to win major trophies, which could elevate his legacy. It also shows he’s not content with merely staying at a big club; he wants tangible success, a narrative that fans and analysts will follow closely.
- **For the season**: United’s performance is now a litmus test for Pochettino’s methods. A return to form could shift the league’s dynamics, altering the title race and the pressure on rivals like Liverpool and Chelsea. Fernandes’ comments add pressure on the manager to deliver results or risk losing his best creative asset.

## What's next
Watch the next match against a top‑four side—United’s performance will be the barometer for Fernandes’ patience. If they secure a win, it could reignite contract talks; a loss might push the player to consider a move. Keep an eye on press conferences for any shift in the club’s stance and for potential transfer rumours that could surface as the season progresses.

*Source: [Fernandes confirms Manchester United contract talks on hold, 'priority is winning'](https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/50560581/bruno-fernandes-manchester-united-premier-league-mauricio-pochettino)*
